neighbours.label: the object of a causative/resultative verb in an urgent or protective action ('to get themselves out of the way', 'Keep your child's vaccines up to date')
fire: As the flood rose, families struggled to get themselves and their pets to higher ground.
When the alarm sounded, workers hurried to get themselves out of the building.
Before the storm hits, make sure to get your children inside.
The guards rushed to get the prisoners back into their cells.
During the fire, neighbors helped to get themselves and the elderly out.
Parents should keep their kids away from the pool when no adult is there.
She shouted at him to get himself out of the road immediately.
Rescuers worked to get the miners up before the tunnel collapsed.
quiet: As the flood rose, families watched the water from their porches.
When the alarm sounded, workers wondered if it was only a drill.
Before the storm hits, the clouds turn dark over the hills.
The guards counted the prisoners in their cells at night.
During the fire, neighbors stood on the street and talked.
Parents often sit by the pool and read while kids swim.
She shouted at him from across the road in the rain.
Rescuers arrived at the mine shortly after the tunnel collapsed.

notes: Probe: 'scurried desperately to get themselves' 0.67; 'rushed to the school' 0.09.
